data.title: UBS acquires 4.8% stake in 360 ONE WAM: What the warrant conversion means for India's wealth market - Decoded
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 23 -- 360 ONE WAM, one of India's largest independent wealth and asset management firms, announced on Thursday that Swiss banking major UBS had acquired a 4.8% stake in the company through the conversion of warrants.

UBS AG had subscribed to 20,502,939 warrants on a preferential basis under an agreement with 360 ONE. The warrants were allotted on July 21, 2025, with 25% of the exercise price paid at the time of allotment. UBS AG has now exercised all the warrants and paid the remaining 75% of the exercise price.

"Pursuant to this, 360 ONE has allotted 2,05,02,939 equity shares to UBS AG, representing approximately a 4.8% equity stake in 360 ONE WAM Ltd," the company said in a regulatory filing.

The move comes as global private banks face increasing competition from domestic players, including Kotak Mahindra Bank's private banking arm and 360 ONE. India is among the world's fastest-growing wealth markets, with nearly a million millionaires and at least 211 billionaires, according to UBS estimates.

In April 2025, the companies announced a partnership under which UBS agreed to sell its Indian onshore wealth management business to 360 ONE for around $32 million, while acquiring warrants representing a 4.95% stake in the Indian firm.

360 ONE WAM is among India's leading wealth and asset management firms, managing assets worth more than Rs.9 lakh crore ($94.1 billion) and serving over 9,000 families and corporate clients. Last month, the company announced that Jefferies India head Aashish Agarwal would take over as its chief executive officer in February.

The company aims to capture a larger share of the market for managing the wealth of India's richest families over the next few years, as demand for asset management services in this segment continues to grow.

India's largest independent wealth manager currently commands nearly 10% of the ultra-high-net-worth market and aims to increase its share to 12%-13%, Co-founder Yatin Shah told Bloomberg in an interview in August.

UBS is a global wealth manager and Switzerland's leading universal bank. It also offers asset management solutions and investment banking services. The bank managed $7.3 trillion in invested assets as of the second quarter of 2026.

The shares have turned volatile recently after an extended rally. So far in October, the stock has declined 3%, following a 12.4% fall in September. Looking further back, the stock witnessed a strong rally between May 2023 and December 2024, gaining around 200%.

On a year-to-date basis, the stock is down 16%, with shares trading at around Rs.997.

data.title: Apple iPhone 17 Pro price drops to Rs.72,050 on Flipkart with exchange and bank offers: Check how the deal works
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 23 -- Apple iPhone 17 Pro buyers can get the 256GB variant for an effective price of Rs.72,050 on Flipkart through an exchange offer and a bank discount. The deal is for those who are willing to swap their eligible Apple iPhone 16 Pro and avail the respective offer from HDFC Bank. The price mentioned is taken from Flipkart's product page as of 23 October.

The iPhone 17 Pro (256GB) comes at Rs.134,900 on the e-commerce platform in Deep Blue. Flipkart is providing Rs.57,850 as an exchange discount on a qualifying iPhone 16 Pro and offering a Rs.5,000 discount from HDFC Bank. The effective price, after these offers, comes down to Rs.72,050, though the actual amount will be contingent on the exchange eligibility, the condition of the device and the terms provided by the bank.

According to Flipkart's product listing, the exchange offer accounts for the largest part of the price reduction. Buyers of an eligible iPhone 16 Pro will get an exchange benefit of up to Rs.57,850. An extra Rs.5,000 discount is offered under the respective offer of HDFC Bank.

The combined benefits reduce the listed price by Rs.62,850. However, the exchange value is dependent on the condition and eligibility of the old device. Buyers should verify the final valuation and bank discount at checkout before placing an order.

There's also an EMI option available on Flipkart for Rs.12,566 per month for 6 months. It is recommended to check the applicable interest rate, processing fees, and other conditions before choosing the payment option.

The Apple iPhone 17 Pro comes with a triple rear camera system and hardware from Apple's Pro-series smartphone lineup. The 256GB version is listed in the Flipkart listings in Deep Blue colour, and there are variants of 512GB and 1TB storage that are also listed at higher prices.

The product page has an average rating of 4.7, with 6,188 ratings. This is the rating as shown on Flipkart and might fluctuate once more users check out the device.

data.title: Infosys Q2 results, dividend 2026 amount announced: Rs.26 per share payout, profit jumps 6.23% YoY - Check record date
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 23 -- Infosys, on Friday, reported a 6.23% annual jump in its consolidated net profit (attributable to owners of the company) to Rs.7832 crore in the September quarter of financial year 2026-27. The IT major also declared an interim dividend of Rs.26 per equity share with a face value of Rs.5 each.

Infosys share price closed marginally higher on Friday, despite the bearish sentiment prevailing across the Indian stock market today. Here are all the details about Infosys Q2 results, dividend announcement and its record date.

The Bengaluru-headquartered IT services firm reported a net profit of Rs.7,823 crore in Q2FY27, which is 6.23% higher than Rs.7,364 crore reported in the year-ago period.

The IT services firm's net revenue from operations stood at Rs.49,244 crore in Q2FY27 against Rs.44,490 crore reported in the year-ago period.

The company's board of directors, on Friday, considered and approved, interim dividend of Rs.26 per share, which is 500% of the stock's face value. It has also announced record date to determine eligibility for the payout and the payment date.

As per Infosys BSE filing, investors must own the stock before record date, fixed November 3, to become eligible for the payout. The announced dividend is scheduled to be paid by November 11.

Its revenue growth stood at 1.2% on a sequential basis ( in constant currency terms), whereas 1.5% on an annual basis (in CC terms). Its operating margin remained stable at 21%. Earnings per share (EPS) growth stood at 8.7% on an annual basis in rupee terms. TCV of large deal wins stood at $5.2 billion, with 62% net new.

In the first half of financial year 2026-27, Infosys' H1 revenues grew at 1.9% on an annual basis (in CC terms) and its operating margin for H1 stood at 21%.

"We had strong large deals of $5.2 billion, including a mega deal of over $2 billion, reinforcing our position as a trusted partner in the marketplace when clients embark on large and complex transformation programs. Our AI revenue was at 10.5% and grew 29% quarter-on-quarter. As enterprises move to AI adoption at scale, the strong growth in AI revenues is a recognition of our differentiated market positioning and client confidence," said Salil Parekh, CEO and MD.

The company kept its revenue growth guidance at 1%-2% in constant currency terms. Whereas, operating margin is likely to remain near 20%-22%. "We delivered operating margins of 21.0% in Q2 amidst heightened volatility. Focus on cost and operational efficiency measures while making the required investments, have led to stable margins," said Jayesh Sanghrajka, CFO

data.title: Infosys beats Q2 estimates, lowers annual revenue forecast
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 23 -- Infosys trimmed its annual revenue growth forecast on Friday despite marginally beating estimates for quarterly revenue after demand from its energy and utility clients picked up.

Revenue at India's second-largest IT services provider rose 10.7% to 492.44 billion rupees ($5.19 billion) in the July-September period.

Analysts on average had estimated revenue of 491.32 billion rupees, according to data compiled by LSEG.

The company revised its revenue growth forecast for the fiscal year ending March 2027 to 1%-2% from its earlier estimate of up 1.5%-3%.

Most analysts had expected the company to downgrade the upper-end of the range to 1.5% to 2.5%.

The rise of AI has hurt India's $315 billion IT industry, forcing companies to overhaul their business models and offer steep discounts.

Despite AI unlocking newer revenue streams, it is challenging the traditional revenue as clients are increasingly tying fees ​to technology-led productivity gains instead of hours worked.

Peers Tata Consultancy Services and HCLTech both met their revenue estimates earlier this week, but their investors cheered AI revenue uptick with their stocks surging.

Revenue from Infosys' energy business, its third-largest revenue contributor, rose 7.3% from a year earlier after stripping out currency fluctuations. The overall revenue rose 1.5%, excluding the currency impact.

The Bengaluru-based tech major's net profit rose 6.2% to 78.23 billion rupees in the three-month period, falling below 79.29 billion rupees expected by analysts, as per LSEG-compiled data.

Deal wins stood at $5.2 billion during the quarter, compared with $3.1 billion in the year-ago quarter.

The company's Mumbai-listed shares closed flat ahead of the results, with a basket of IT stocks dropping 0.3%.

data.title: BlueStone tweaks product mix, store model as gold prices reshape demand
data.description:
Bengaluru, Oct. 23 -- BlueStone Jewellery and Lifestyle Ltd is reworking its entry-level jewellery offerings and testing new retail formats as rising gold prices reshape customer demand. The strategy comes as the retailer's September-quarter (Q2FY27) revenue rose 43.9% year-on-year, even as same-store sales growth moderated from the preceding quarter. Its shares fell about 11% on the BSE on Friday.

The company's consolidated revenue came in at Rs.745 crore, matching Bloomberg's estimate. Its consolidated net loss stood at Rs.4.37 crore, wider than the estimated loss of Rs.3.23 crore, though narrowing significantly from a net loss of Rs.52.10 crore in the corresponding period of the previous fiscal year. Meanwhile, operational efficiency improved as Ebitda margin expanded to 13.2% in Q2FY27 from about 8.4% in Q2FY26.

BlueStone is adjusting its product mix as rising gold prices weigh on affordability. It has redesigned its entry-level range, is seeing greater acceptance of 14-carat jewellery, and is considering testing nine-carat products. The company is also expanding its store network and piloting a franchise-owned, franchise-operated model to reach more customers.

Same-store sales growth (SSSG) was 28% in the September quarter, compared with 39% in the June quarter. The company attributed part of the moderation to a shift in the festive calendar, with Navratri falling in October this year compared with September last year.

"I wouldn't call it muted," founder and chief executive officer Gaurav Singh Kushwaha said about the SSSG performance. He said the shift in festive dates was one reason not to read too much into the sequential moderation, adding that the company focuses on longer-term trends in customer behaviour. For the first half of FY27, SSSG stood at 32.9%.

The retailer's focus on entry-level products reflects the pressure that rising gold prices have put on affordability. "Over the past year, a key focus area has been our entry-level price points, where gold price inflation dislocated our offering," the company said in its management commentary. "Our redesigned range is now taking more shelf space in our stores, and this quarter we saw early signs of that effort paying off."

The changes helped bring more new customers into the business, though average order value moderated to Rs.77,290 from Rs.78,081 in the June quarter. "The average order value definitely falls. That is not necessarily a bad thing," Kushwaha said, arguing that the average ticket size alone was not a sufficient measure of the strategy's success.

BlueStone is also exploring lower-purity gold jewellery to offer customers more price points. Kushwaha declined to disclose the revenue contribution of 14-carat products, citing competitive reasons. On nine-carat jewellery, he said the company did not yet have firm conviction about the opportunity, but added that it was "worth testing out". A wider rollout has not been confirmed.

BlueStone crossed one million customers during the quarter, reaching 1.024 million, up 19.3% year-on-year. Repeat customers contributed 56.3% of revenue, compared with 51.4% a year earlier. The company said a growing customer base and higher repeat-purchase frequency could support longer-term growth at individual stores as they mature.

The company added 27 stores during the quarter, taking its network to 379 across 146 cities. It aims to reach 400-410 stores by the end of FY27, with expansion spanning new markets and additional stores in cities where it already operates.

BlueStone is also testing a franchise-owned, franchise-operated (FOFO) model, under which franchise partners provide the capital and run stores themselves. "I think FOFO is not something that we have tried so far," Kushwaha said. He said the company believed local ownership and operational involvement could improve performance in selected locations, but would assess the results before deciding whether to expand the model.

The company has historically used a franchise-owned, company-operated model for some outlets. Kushwaha said most of these stores are expected to transition to company-operated formats over time as agreements expire, with the process unfolding over roughly five years.

BlueStone is targeting revenue of around Rs.12,000 crore by FY30, up from Rs.2,441 crore in FY26. Kushwaha said many of the company's stores were still relatively young, with revenue expected to rise as they mature. This could help the company generate operating leverage against its fixed costs.

On demand, Kushwaha said it was too early to draw firm conclusions about the festive and wedding season since many major shopping days lie ahead. However, early demand remains in line with the company's expectations, he added. He also cautioned against drawing direct parallels with other consumer categories, saying jewellery had its own cycles and did not necessarily move in tandem with broader discretionary spending.

BlueStone is also looking to strengthen the link between online discovery and physical stores as more than 80% of its sales originate online, according to its earnings release. Kushwaha emphasized that online and offline channels should not be viewed in isolation. Because fine jewellery is a high-consideration purchase, he explained, customers can research designs online but often want to see a piece in person before buying.

BlueStone's board approved a private placement of non-convertible debentures (NCDs) to raise up to Rs.300 crore. Kushwaha said a significant portion of the proceeds would be used to refinance high-cost debt, with the rest available for other business requirements.

data.title: Tata Motors posts Q2 profit on strong commercial vehicle demand
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 23 -- India's Tata Motors on Friday posted a quarterly profit compared to a loss a year earlier, helped by healthy demand for commercial vehicles.

The automaker reported a profit of 21.38 billion rupees ($225.19 million) for the July to September quarter, compared with a loss of 10.21 billion rupees a year earlier. The profit included a one-time gain of 2.18 billion rupees.

Commercial vehicle demand remained resilient in the quarter, led by steady freight movement, government-led infrastructure activity and healthy fleet utilisation, supporting growth in the medium and heavy truck segment, a key revenue generator for Tata Motors.

Total revenue from operations rose 41.9% to 239.30 billion rupees, helped by a 42% increase in wholesale sales, with growth in domestic and export volumes.

The commercial vehicle maker rolled out three price hikes this year, with the latest in September when it raised prices by up to 1%.

However, rising raw material prices more than offset the benefits of the recent price hikes and continued to weigh on the company's margins. Core margin for the second quarter was at 11.7%, down 90 basis points from a year earlier.

"With H1FY27 volumes up 35%, we remain well positioned for a robust FY27, even as growth rates are expected to moderate in the second half against a higher base," Girish Wagh, managing director and CEO of Tata Motors, said in a statement.

Tata Motors is part of India's Tata Group, which is caught in a power struggle over control of the holding company and whether it should go public.

data.title: SBI data leak: This is what India's largest public sector bank told customers as 3,897 records flagged in cyber incident
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 23 -- State Bank of India (SBI) has begun individually notifying customers whose information was identified in a suspected cyber incident, while assuring account holders that their funds remain safe as the bank investigates the possible exposure of personal data.

"Further to our earlier post regarding the recent cyber incident, the Bank has individually informed all customers, whose data was identified as being involved, through email and/or WhatsApp," SBI said in an advisory to customers on Friday.

The bank reiterated that "your account balances and funds are safe with us" and urged customers to remain alert while using digital banking services.

In its advisory, SBI asked customers to exercise caution when handling sensitive banking information.

"Customers are advised to follow safe digital banking practices, never share their OTP, PIN or password with anyone, and remain vigilant against suspicious calls, messages and emails," the advisory said.

The communication follows the bank's disclosure of a suspected data leak involving customer records reportedly found on the dark web.

According to SBI's stock exchange filing, a preliminary examination of around 3.75 lakh records identified 3,897 records containing personally identifiable information.

The information reportedly included customers' names, registered mobile numbers, dates of birth, email IDs and residential addresses. The records also contained branch and customer identification details, along with metadata associated with loan and lead records.

The identification of personal information in the records does not, by itself, establish that customers' bank accounts or funds have been accessed or compromised.

SBI received alerts about the suspected exposure on October 16 from its threat-intelligence service provider, the Defence Cyber Agency and the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In).

Following the alerts, the bank activated its cyber incident response and containment protocols. It also appointed an independent cybersecurity agency empanelled with CERT-In to investigate the incident.

The investigation is expected to establish the authenticity and extent of the information that may have been exposed, its possible source and the risks associated with the incident.

SBI has said the incident has had no material impact on its core business operations, financial performance or business continuity. The bank has also reassured customers that their account balances and funds are safe.

However, the investigation is ongoing, and the extent and implications of the suspected data exposure are yet to be fully established.

Customers should avoid sharing one-time passwords (OTPs), PINs or passwords with anyone, including callers claiming to represent the bank. They should also exercise caution with unexpected links, messages and emails requesting personal or financial information.

Customers who receive a notification from SBI should verify that it is genuine before acting on it. Any suspicious communication or suspected unauthorised transaction should be reported to the bank through its official channels.

data.title: Paid Rs.1.15 lakh to move goods to Nagaland, got damaged TV and 23 missing items; what did consumer commission order?
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 23 -- A woman who paid Rs.1.15 lakh to shift her household belongings from Delhi to Nagaland received her consignment nearly two months late, with 23 items missing and several others damaged, including her LED television and air conditioner.

The South Delhi District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has now directed the packers and movers and Urban Company to pay her a combined compensation of Rs.3.5 lakh for deficient services, mental agony and harassment, according to The Economic Times report.

The complainant, identified as Longchar, had booked the relocation service through Urban Company in September 2020. She hired the moving company to transport her household belongings, including furniture, electronic appliances, fixtures and her car, from Delhi to Dimapur in Nagaland.

The household goods were loaded onto the moving company's truck on September 20, 2020. However, the delivery was considerably delayed. While Longchar received her car on October 23, 2020, the household belongings reached her only on November 19, almost two months after the shipment was dispatched.

The delivery was also incomplete. On checking the consignment, she discovered that the truck contained only 70 of the 93 household items that had been loaded for transportation. The remaining 23 items were missing.

Several of the delivered belongings were damaged as well. Longchar alleged that her air conditioner had arrived in a broken condition and was beyond repair. Her LED television was damaged, while crockery, utensils, electronic appliances and other electrical goods were also found broken during unpacking.

According to Longchar, the moving company initially refused to accept responsibility for the damaged goods and instead blamed other parties.

Following repeated efforts, the movers reportedly agreed to pay Rs.25,000 for the damaged air conditioner. They also assured her that compensation for the other damaged products would be provided after the remaining belongings were delivered.

The company further promised to send the 23 missing items through a courier service. However, Longchar told the commission that she never received the promised shipment.

Aggrieved by the delay, missing belongings and damage, she approached the consumer commission seeking a refund of the Rs.1.15 lakh paid for the service. She also demanded Rs.4 lakh in damages, Rs.1.50 lakh for financial losses, Rs.50,000 for mental tension and trauma, and Rs.60,000 towards litigation expenses. Her total claim amounted to Rs.7.75 lakh.

The commission issued notices to the packers and movers and Urban Company. However, no representative appeared on behalf of the moving company.

Urban Company contested the complaint, stating that it operates a managed marketplace through which customers can access services offered by independent third-party providers. It argued that it had no liability to pay or reimburse any amount to the complainant.

The commission, however, did not accept this argument. It examined the documents submitted by Longchar, which showed that the moving company had a service rating of 4.45 on Urban Company's platform.

The panel observed that the complainant would have considered the service provider's rating before deciding to book its services.

"Hence the plea of OP-3 (Urban Company) that it is merely an intermediary who provides a common platform from where the consumers can engage the services of third party cannot be absolved of its liability," the panel said, as per ET.

Taking into account the delayed delivery, damaged air conditioner and LED television, and the 23 missing household items, the commission held the moving company "grossly deficient in service".

After examining the complaint and the evidence, the South Delhi District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission directed both companies to compensate Longchar.

The commission directed the packers and movers to pay Rs.3 lakh as compensation for deficient services and the damage and loss of household belongings. It also ordered Urban Company to pay Rs.50,000 towards compensation for mental agony, harassment and litigation costs. Both parties were instructed to make the payments within three months from the date of the order.

data.title: Sen. Blumenthal seeks answers from Tether over payments to firm founded by ex-White House crypto adviser
data.description:
Sen. Richard Blumenthal said he wants answers from Tether following reports that the stablecoin issuer paid millions of dollars to a consulting firm started by former White House crypto adviser Bo Hines and his father amid negotiations to pass stablecoin legislation into law.

The Connecticut Democrat said that relationship raised legal and ethical concerns, in a letter sent to Tether and Hines.

"Tether’s alleged multimillion-dollar payment to a firm controlled by the White House official primarily responsible for cryptocurrency policy implicates federal ethics, anticorruption, and lobbying laws," Blumenthal said on Thursday.

Last week, The Wall Street Journal reported that Tether had started a business relationship with Nxum — a consulting firm started by Bo Hines and his father — weeks after Hines took the helm as the White House's top crypto advisor. During Hines' time at the White House, he played a pivotal role in passing the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins, or GENIUS Act, which created the first federal regulatory framework for stablecoins.

Tether, which issues the world's largest stablecoin, became an advocate for the GENIUS Act and, through it, launched the U.S.-based version of its flagship stablecoin, called USAT.

A Tether spokesperson told The Block that the company is reviewing the letter. "Tether is aware of the allegations reported in The Wall Street Journal that form the basis of Senator Blumenthal’s letter," the spokesperson said. "External counsel previously conducted an in-depth internal investigation into the matter, which found no evidence of wrongdoing."

Lawmakers, including Blumenthal, have repeatedly scrutinized Tether over the past year. Last month, Blumenthal released findings of an investigation that found that Tether had become central in "Iran's shadow banking system" and the financing activities of terrorist groups. Tether has pushed back and said it helps authorities find bad actors.

In Blumenthal's latest letter, he asked Tether to provide records involving the stablecoin issuer's business dealings with Nxum as well as with Hines.

Blumenthal also sent a letter on Thursday to Nxum. Harry Jung, the now-former deputy director of the President's Council of Advisors for Digital Assets who worked with Hines, is now at Nxum, according to his X account.

Leadership at the council is also absent now following the departure of Patrick Witt last week after his detail expired. Witt did not say where he would be going next, but said in a post on X that he looked forward to advancing his mission in the private sector.

data.title: Ather Energy, TVS Motor, Bajaj Auto, Tata Motors PV shares: Can Delhi's pollution curbs change game for auto-EV stocks?
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 23 -- Delhi's air pollution control measures are set to tighten from November 1, with multiple curbs including, restrictions on non BS-VI vehicles. The stricter curbs could provide a boost to the EV theme, potentially creating opportunities for auto companies operating in the electric mobility space like Ather Energy, TVS Motor Company, Bajaj Auto, Tata Motors (Passenger Vehicles), according to experts.

Under Delhi's air pollution measures, there will be restrictions on vehicle use, higher parking charges, and other enforcement to reduce emissions across the National Capital Region (NCR). One of the significant curbs is restriction of vehicles registered outside Delhi that do not meet Bharat Stage VI (BS VI) emission norms.

While these measures aim to curb pollution, could they also fuel a shift in the fortunes of auto and EV stocks? Let's understand from experts

The direct push to EV adoption will be modest due to the Delhi pollution curbs, according to Gaurav Garg, Head - Research, Lemonn, who sees conventional commercial vehicles as the near-term winners instead of EV stocks.

"The bigger lever is Delhi EV Policy 2.0. From 1 January 2027, it allows only electric autos and light goods vehicles to be newly registered in Delhi. Delhi already leads on adoption: EVs were 12.7% of its FY26 registrations, against roughly 8-9% nationally. For stocks, expect sentiment, not earnings," explained Garg.

Echoing the view that the restrictions are temporary rather than indicative of a permanent ban, Rubina Singla, founder - Equitrust Solutions, highlights that such actions "reinforce the broader regulatory push towards cleaner mobility in the NCR" and may create incremental replacement demand.

"Two-wheelers account for a significantly larger share of personal mobility in Delhi-NCR. Any friction on older ICE two-wheelers (entry restrictions + higher parking costs for non-EVs) creates a larger addressable replacement pool. The price point and daily-use nature of two-wheelers make the switch to electric relatively easier and faster for consumers compared to passenger vehicles," explained Singla.

Bajaj Auto, through its Chetak EV portfolio, is well-positioned to capture the replacement demand in the electric scooter segment. Ather Energy and TVS Motor, have strong and growing electric two-wheeler franchises.

Tata Motors (Passenger Vehicles) and Mahindra & Mahindra may benefit due to their EV portfolio in the passenger electric vehicle adoption.

"These two remain the strongest pure-play EV passenger vehicle players in India. While the immediate impact of the non-BS-VI entry curb is more pronounced for two-wheelers, any acceleration in the shift away from older ICE cars in Delhi-NCR will favour Tata and Mahindra given their existing EV product pipelines and market share in the electric car segment," explains Singla.

The e-two-wheeler market in Delhi-NCR is still growing. Delhi has around 8% of national volume in e-cars and e-goods carriers.

Whereas, Delhi Transport Corporation (DTC), runs India's largest electric fleet, with over 4,000 buses and about 3,300 more planned, highlighted Gaurav Garg to reaffirm that companies manufacturing electric buses, e-autos, electric small commercial vehicles (e-SVs) and electric cares are likely to be more sensitive to these curbs.

data.title: Top telecom shares to buy: Bharti Airtel, Vodafone Idea, Indus Towers by Ambit Capital with new stock target price
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 23 -- Indian telecom stocks could be poised for further gains as tariff hikes, rising data consumption and opportunities in digital infrastructure strengthen the sector's growth outlook, according to Ambit Capital. In a recent research report, the brokerage reiterated its positive stance on the sector, forecasting a 15% mobile tariff hike in December 2026, followed by 12% increases every two years over the next decade.

Ambit Capital named Bharti Airtel its top sector pick and maintained BUY ratings on Bharti Airtel, Indus Towers, Vodafone Idea and Bharti Hexacom. The brokerage believes improving pricing discipline, operating leverage and diversification into data centres could support earnings growth, although execution risks and potential regulatory changes remain important monitorables.

"Our positive view of the sector rests on our expectation of pricing discipline after Jio's listing and the government's desire for a three-private-player industry structure. Bharti Airtel is our top sector pick," said the brokerage.

Bharti Airtel: BUY | | Target price: Rs.2,732 | Upside: 44%

Indus Towers: BUY | Target price: Rs.532 | Upside: 39%

Vodafone Idea: BUY | Target price: Rs.18.7 | Upside: 62%

Bharti Hexacom: BUY | Target price: Rs.2,130 | Upside: 31%

The brokerage's positive outlook rests on its expectation that telecom operators will continue raising tariffs to improve profitability. It believes the industry's current economics remain challenging, with pre-tax return on capital employed at approximately 10% in FY26, below the cost of capital.

Ambit Capital expects the need for Vodafone Idea to improve its financial position, Reliance Industries' objective of generating returns for Jio Platforms investors, and the sector's investment requirements to support periodic tariff increases. It expects a 15% hike in December 2026, followed by biennial increases of 12%.

The report also highlighted the potential of rising mobile data consumption. Handset upgrades and continued 5G network investments could support higher usage, allowing telecom operators to raise prices while offering more data. The brokerage noted that Airtel's decision to remove its entry-level 1.5GB-per-day plan in August 2026 could lift average revenue per user (ARPU) by 4.4%.

Ambit Capital said, "Consumer handset upgrades and telco 5G network investments will keep per capita data consumption rising, as in the past. This builds a compelling case for telcos to implement biennial 12% price increases over the next decade alongside more generous data allowances."

Beyond mobile tariffs, the brokerage sees data centres and private cloud services as potential growth drivers. Airtel has outlined plans to expand its data-centre capacity from 240 megawatts to 1 gigawatt by the end of the decade. Edge data centres could also create opportunities for tower companies, although power and water availability remain key execution risks.

On the risks, Ambit Capital cautioned that satellite communications could challenge incremental monetisation by telecom operators. However, it believes regulatory safeguards and sovereignty considerations favour incumbent telecom companies. A potential government preference for introducing a new telecom operator also remains a risk to its sector view.

Ambit Capital expects Bharti Airtel and Reliance Jio to deliver revenue compound annual growth rates (CAGRs) of 16% and 15%, respectively, between FY26 and FY29. For Airtel, it forecasts a 15% revenue CAGR and a 31% adjusted profit after tax CAGR over the same period.

The brokerage believes the Street could be underestimating Airtel's operating leverage and financial growth. Its revenue estimates for FY29 are 7% above Bloomberg consensus, while its profit after tax estimate is 11% higher. It expects Airtel's consolidated revenue to rise to Rs.3,254 billion in FY29, from Rs.2,110 billion in FY26.

For Bharti Hexacom, Ambit Capital projects a 13% revenue CAGR and a 30% earnings-per-share CAGR between FY26 and FY29. It expects Vodafone Idea to begin curbing subscriber losses from FY28, supported by network investments, customer retention and tariff repair. The brokerage also sees scope to upgrade Vodafone Idea's EBITDA margin estimates for FY28 and FY29.

Data centres are another opportunity, but Ambit Capital stressed that returns will depend on execution and customer mix. The report noted that payback periods have lengthened as competition and investment commitments have increased.

Ambit Capital said, "Execution risk, rather than finding the right customer, is the big risk, with water and power linkages emerging as choke points. DCs have become a 'red ocean' with payback periods stretching to 11 years currently versus 4-4.5 years pre-Covid."

Overall, Ambit Capital's investment thesis is built on higher tariffs, earnings growth and the expansion of digital infrastructure. While Bharti Airtel remains its preferred telecom stock, the brokerage has also assigned BUY ratings to Indus Towers, Vodafone Idea and Bharti Hexacom, with the outlook dependent on tariff implementation, execution and the regulatory environment.

data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 23 -- Brokerage firm PL Capital has initiated coverage on newly listed stock Sai Lifesciences, with a 'Buy' rating and a target price of Rs.1,620 per share, seeing an upside potential up to 16% over the current market price of Rs.1,394.

PL Capital believes the company is well positioned to benefit from increasing pharmaceutical outsourcing, a deep commercial pipeline and capacity expansion, supported by its integrated contract research, development and manufacturing organisation (CRDMO) platform.

In its report, the brokerage further said that Sai Life Sciences has established an integrated platform spanning drug discovery, development and manufacturing, enabling it to support pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies across a molecule's lifecycle.

The brokerage sees large pharmaceutical companies as a key near-term growth driver, while the conversion of late-stage molecules into commercial manufacturing and rising business from existing customers could strengthen revenue visibility.

PL Capital has initiated coverage on Sai Life Sciences with a 'Buy' rating and a target price of Rs.1,620 per share, valuing the company at 55 times its estimated price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple for September 2028. At the current market price of Rs.1,390, the target implies an upside potential of approximately 16.5%.

The brokerage noted that the stock is trading at around 29 times enterprise value to EBITDA (EV/EBITDA) on a pre-Ind AS basis and 48 times its estimated P/E for September 2028. Despite the valuation premium, PL Capital believes the company's integrated business model, expanding commercial pipeline and growth opportunities in complex chemistry and new drug modalities support its long-term investment case.

PL Capital believes Sai Life Sciences' integrated discovery-to-commercialisation model gives it an advantage in retaining customers and increasing its share of business as drug candidates progress through clinical development and into commercial production. More than 90% of the company's revenue comes from repeat customers, reflecting its established relationships and ability to support complex pharmaceutical programmes.

PL Capital expects the company's revenue to grow at around 21% CAGR between FY26 and FY29, supported by a steady flow of projects moving from discovery to development and commercial manufacturing. It believes the deep pipeline and increasing wallet share from existing customers could improve revenue visibility over the coming years.

Sai Life Sciences shares have posted mixed performance in the short term, rising 0.40% over the past week but declining 13.33% over the past month, indicating recent selling pressure. The monthly decline comes despite the stock maintaining strong gains over a longer period.

On a year-to-date (YTD) basis, Sai Life Sciences shares have surged 54.96%, while the stock has gained 56.36% over the past year.

data.title: ideaForge Technology terminates US joint venture agreement with First Breach
data.description:
Drone technology company ideaForge Technology Ltd on Friday (October 23) said its wholly owned US subsidiary, ideaForge Technology Inc., has terminated its joint venture agreement with First Breach Inc. of the United States, as the proposed deal did not close before the agreed deadline.

The termination was also based on mutual discussions between the two parties. The joint venture agreement was signed on September 23, 2025, to establish First Forge Technology Inc. and jointly undertake the licensing, sourcing, designing, engineering, manufacturing and distribution of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in the US.

The termination agreement was executed on October 23, 2026. Under its terms, both parties have irrevocably released and waived all claims against each other. Non-compete and non-solicitation obligations under the original agreement will not survive the termination.

The company said the proposed joint venture was never implemented because the closing did not occur before the expiry of the long-stop date. Consequently, no shares were issued and no capital contribution was made under the joint venture agreement.

ideaForge said the termination would have no impact on the management or control of the listed company. The transaction does not fall under related-party transactions.

Shares of ideaForge Technology Ltd ended at ₹646.65, down by ₹32.90, or 4.84%, on the BSE.

data.title: Norwegian Sells Most of Its Europe Cruises to Americans. Why That's a Problem. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Mariapaula Gonzalez

American travelers have grown increasingly wary of traveling to Europe as the wars in Ukraine and Iran show no end in sight. That's a big problem for Norwegian Cruise Line, which relies heavily on the U.S. market to fill up its European itineraries.

J.P. Morgan's Matthew Boss says he is concerned about the drop in U.S. demand for European trips. He predicts Norwegian's constant-currency yield growth — the average amount of money it makes from each available cabin bed a day, stripping out currency swings — will likely remain stagnant rather than grow in 2027. That forecast is well below Wall Street's consensus estimate for 0.8% constant-currency yield growth next year.

In the June quarter, Norwegian's constant-currency yield fell 2.6% year over year. But management saw this as a positive, since they previously projected a 3.6% decline.

Though net yields could rebound in the second half of 2027, the drop in cruise trip demand will still likely overshadow that potential recovery, Boss wrote in a note Friday. He downgraded the stock to Underweight from Neutral on Friday while trimming its price target to $11 from $13.

Norwegian Cruise Line didn't respond to a request for comment.

Geopolitical conflicts have remained a challenge for Norwegian, given that 85% of Europe itineraries for the cruise line operator were travelers coming from the U.S., Boss noted. That's the highest percentage of U.S. visitors to Europe across J.P. Morgan's cruise coverage.

Norwegian Cruise Line stock dropped 3.8% to $14.95 Friday. Shares have fallen 30% this year through Thursday's close.

Of the 29 analysts polled by FactSet, 18 have a Hold rating while two now recommend selling shares.

Rising oil prices have been another key headwind for Norwegian stock and other cruise operators. The recent climb in crude oil prices have reignited worries that these companies could see their profits drop in the final quarter of the year.

Shares of Royal Caribbean fell 3.1% on Friday, while Carnival Corp. and Viking Holdings dropped 3.6% and 2.9%, respectively. Meanwhile, the S&P 500 dipped 0.2%.

Write to Mariapaula Gonzalez at mariapaula.gonzalez@barrons.com

The upgraded mechanism introduces unified governance under JUST DAO, a minimum $50 million treasury reserve for risk mitigation, emergency redemptions, andâ€¦ pic.twitter.com/eihe1pSzcM

Oct 23, 2026

JST Info

JUST is a decentralized finance (DeFi) ecosystem on the TRON blockchain, launched in August 2020. It offers a suite of DeFi products, primarily centered around JustStable, a decentralized stablecoin lending platform. The ecosystem aims to provide a comprehensive range of DeFi services, creating a complete DeFi ecosystem on TRON.

JUST’s platform includes various products like JustStable, JustLend, JustSwap, JustLink, and tokenized cross-chain assets. Users can deposit collateral tokens, like TRON (TRX), to mint USDJ, a stablecoin pegged to the US dollar. This process involves creating a collateralized debt position (CDP). JustLend allows for liquidity provision and low-interest loans, JustSwap facilitates trustless token swaps, and JustLink provides decentralized oracle services.

JST is the native governance token of the JUST ecosystem, circulating since May 2020. It serves multiple functions on the platform, including paying interest, maintaining the platform, and participating in governance decisions. These decisions involve setting crucial parameters like interest rates and minimum collateralization ratios. JST plays a central role in the operation and governance of the JUST ecosystem.

data.title: This SpaceX Bear Flips To Being A Bull On The Firm's AI Developments, Sees 70% Stock Upside
data.description:
Key points:
  • PhillipCapital executed a rare double upgrade on SpaceX stock, shifting its rating from ‘sell’ to ‘buy’ and tripling its price target to $250. 
  • The bullish reversal follows SpaceX's third-quarter report featuring $14.58 billion in revenue, adjusted earnings of $0.45 per share, and its first-ever profitability as a public company. 
  • Growth was primarily driven by the company's "super intelligence" (SI) AI cloud services, surging connectivity demand from aviation and Starshield contracts.

Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (SpaceX) shares gained 1.5% on Friday after investment firm PhillipCapital completely reversed its bearish position, upgrading the company's shares from ‘sell’ to ‘buy’.

The bullish outlook was primarily driven by SpaceX’s first-ever quarterly profit as a publicly traded entity. For the third quarter, the Elon Musk-led aerospace and artificial intelligence enterprise reported adjusted earnings of $0.45 per share on revenue of $14.58 billion, comfortably outperforming market expectations.

PhillipCapital also hiked its price target from $75 to $250, implying a gain of nearly 73% from the stock's Thursday close of $147.06.

The Growth Catalysts Behind The Surge

In a research note published Friday, PhillipCapital analyst Glenn Thum explained that the sudden shift into profitability was propelled by artificial intelligence or super intelligence (SI) scaling.

The company's branded "super intelligence" cloud operations benefited from higher rental pricing agreements, while Cursor contributed $608 million beginning in mid-August.

Meanwhile, SpaceX’s enterprise and government revenue jumped 91% year-over-year, driven heavily by new commercial aviation installations and vital Starshield contract deployments.

However, Thum also warned that full-year 2027 revenue could trail behind projections based on annualized first-quarter guidance. He warned that scaling the company's heavy compute infrastructure will face friction, citing power availability and cooling capabilities as critical operational constraints.

SPCX Stock: Retail View

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits was ‘extremely bullish’ with ‘high’ message volumes.

SPCX stock has lost about 9% since its June listing.

data.title: Ionis partner Roche announces new Phase 3 data showing sefaxersen significantly reduced proteinuria in people with IgA nephropathy (IgAN)
data.description:
Ionis Pharmaceuticals, Inc. () partner Roche announced today late-breaking oral presentation data from the ongoing Phase 3 IMAgINATION study in adults with primary IgA nephropathy (IgAN) receiving optimized standard of care, demonstrating that investigational sefaxersen achieved a statistically significant and clinically meaningful 43.1% reduction in proteinuria (95% confidence interval [CI]: 32.5 - 52.0, P<0.0001), relative to placebo at 37 weeks, as measured by 24-hour urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR). Proteinuria is a key indicator of kidney damage and a reduction in UPCR is strongly associated with the preservation of long-term kidney function. Results presented at the American Society of Nephrology (ASN) Kidney Week 2026 also showed that, among patients with baseline hematuria (blood in urine), a greater proportion of patients achieved hematuria resolution at Week 37 with sefaxersen versus placebo.

"These data support our belief that sefaxersen is uniquely positioned to treat IgA nephropathy, demonstrating significant and clinically meaningful reduction in proteinuria and offering the potential to help reduce the need for long-term dialysis or kidney transplantation,” said Brett P. Monia, Ph.D., chief executive officer, Ionis. “Sefaxersen is a powerful example of the broad impact of Ionis' innovative science, and based on these results, we believe it has the potential to be an important new treatment option for people living with IgA nephropathy."

The treatment effect in all prespecified subgroups was consistent with the clinically meaningful reductions in proteinuria shown in the primary endpoint results. Sefaxersen was well tolerated with a safety profile consistent with the previously reported Phase 2 study, exhibiting no new safety signals.

Sefaxersen is an investigational once-monthly subcutaneous injection designed to enable self-administration for people with IgAN. The IMAgINATION study will continue as a blinded study to evaluate the change in kidney function over two years, as measured by estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) at week 105. Roche will share data with health authorities, with the goal of bringing this treatment to patients as soon as possible.

Typically diagnosed before the age of 40, IgAN affects at least 25 adults per million worldwide each year. IgAN, also known as Berger’s disease, is a chronic and progressive autoimmune disease that leads to end-stage kidney disease in up to 50% of patients within 20 years of diagnosis. It is the most common form of primary glomerulonephritis (inflammation of the tiny filters, glomeruli, in the kidneys) and is a major cause of chronic kidney disease as well as kidney failure.

Roche licensed sefaxersen from Ionis for the treatment of complement-mediated diseases. Under the terms of the agreement, Ionis received an upfront payment, license fee and development milestone payments and is eligible to receive regulatory and sales milestone payments as well as tiered royalties on net sales of sefaxersen.

About sefaxersen

Sefaxersen, an investigational, highly specific liver-directed antisense oligonucleotide that inhibits factor B production, is the first RNA-targeted therapy for IgA nephropathy (IgAN). Serum complement factor B levels are elevated in people with IgAN. Sefaxersen is designed to provide sustained control of the alternative complement pathway, an important pathway in IgAN, enabling once-monthly subcutaneous dosing and is intended for self-administration in people with IgAN.

About the IMAgINATION Study

IMAgINATION (NCT05797610) is a Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of subcutaneous sefaxersen, an investigational antisense inhibitor of complement factor B, in patients with primary IgA nephropathy at high risk of progression. The study enrolled 459 people, who are randomized 1:1 to receive sefaxersen or placebo for 105 weeks. Participants may switch to open-label treatment after week 105 at the investigator's discretion or after the common-close timepoint, whichever occurs first. The primary endpoint of the study is the change from baseline in the urine protein-to-creatinine ratio at 37 weeks.

About IgA Nephropathy (IgAN)

IgAN, also known as Berger’s disease, is a serious, chronic and progressive autoimmune kidney disease affecting at least 25 adults per million worldwide each year and is typically diagnosed before the age of 40 years. In IgAN, immune complexes deposit in the kidneys, which activates the complement system’s alternative pathway, leading to inflammation and subsequent kidney damage. It is the most common form of primary glomerulonephritis (inflammation of kidney glomeruli) and remains a leading cause of kidney failure, with up to 50% of patients experiencing end-stage kidney disease within 20 years of diagnosis. Many current therapies aim to reduce protein levels in the urine and control blood pressure to slow progression of the disease.

Updated KDIGO 2025 guidelines* highlight the need to address both the underlying immune-mediated causes of IgAN and the downstream consequences of kidney damage. While new therapies have expanded treatment options, important unmet needs remain, including improved long-term preservation of kidney function and more targeted approaches that address key drivers of disease progression.

About Ionis Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

For more than three decades, Ionis has invented medicines that bring better futures to people with serious diseases. Ionis currently has marketed medicines and a leading pipeline in neurology, cardiometabolic disease and select areas of high patient need. As the pioneer in RNA-targeted medicines, Ionis continues to drive innovation in RNA therapies in addition to advancing new approaches in gene editing. A deep understanding of disease biology and industry-leading technology propels our work, coupled with a passion and urgency to deliver life-changing advances for patients. To learn more about Ionis, visit Ionis.com and follow us on X (Twitter), LinkedIn and Instagram.

Ionis Forward-looking Statements

This press release includes forward-looking statements regarding Ionis' business and the therapeutic and commercial potential of sefaxersen, our commercial medicines, additional medicines in development and technologies and our expectations regarding development and regulatory milestones. Any statement describing Ionis' goals, expectations, financial or other projections, intentions or beliefs is a forward-looking statement and should be considered an at-risk statement.
